headline: High-risk shared-workspace pair: Windsurf’s local filesystem/MCP and broad egress can leak or corrupt Dexter’s financial workflows by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dexter writes to .dexter/scratchpad and uses autonomous execution, while Windsurf reads/writes workspace files, uses clipboard/MCP, and supports per-window shared state via local filesystem. That creates a plausible instruction-injection bridge if Dexter outputs are copied or stored where Windsurf parses them as content. The pathway is interaction-based and not blocked by default.
conditions: IF Dexter output is placed in a shared workspace or scratchpad that Windsurf reads
IF Windsurf treats file or clipboard content as actionable instructions
mitigations: Keep Dexter scratchpad outside Windsurf workspace
Disable clipboard-based handoff between agents
Require manual review of any Dexter-generated text before Windsurf consumes it
Use separate OS users or directories for each agent
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to shared files

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dexter touches financial and market data and has broad network egress to multiple APIs. Windsurf reads workspace files, uses MCP servers, and also has broad egress. If they share a workspace or files, sensitive financial material can flow from Dexter into Windsurf and onward to third-party services without a strong default barrier, making leakage plausible and potentially irreversible.
conditions: IF Dexter stores financial or market data in files accessible to Windsurf
IF Windsurf forwards workspace content to its model proxy or MCP-connected services
mitigations: Store Dexter data in a directory Windsurf cannot read
Disable MCP servers for shared workspaces
Use separate API keys and accounts per agent
Redact financial data before any Windsurf ingestion
requires-engineering: enforce workspace-level access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write files and use broad network egress; Windsurf also modifies git state and supports multiple instances with shared local-filesystem state. Dexter’s autonomous execution plus Windsurf’s command execution can race on the same workspace or repository, causing conflicting writes or git corruption by default unless explicitly isolated.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or workspace
IF either agent commits or rewrites files without external locking
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate checkout
Pause one agent while the other writes git state
Use branch-per-agent workflows
Avoid auto-commit or auto-merge settings
requires-engineering: add file-locking around shared paths

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dexter’s autonomous outputs can become inputs to Windsurf, which has command execution and MCP access. Windsurf may act on Dexter-produced facts or plans without verification, so a mistaken or manipulated Dexter output can cascade into incorrect code changes or terminal actions. The interaction is plausible, but not proven to be default-authoritative.
conditions: IF Windsurf consumes Dexter-generated text as task instructions
IF Windsurf executes commands or MCP actions without independent verification
mitigations: Require human approval for Dexter-to-Windsurf handoffs
Add a verification step before any command execution
Limit Dexter outputs to summaries, not directives
Log and diff all proposed actions before execution
requires-engineering: implement structured handoff schemas

E_compliance.rationale: Dexter explicitly touches financial data and market data, while Windsurf handles open files and workspace files with broad egress. If regulated financial records or customer data are placed into Windsurf’s workspace, retention and residency obligations may diverge from Dexter’s research workflow. The profiles do not show a specific residency mismatch, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF regulated financial or customer data is stored in Windsurf-accessible files
IF the operator requires retention or residency controls not enforced by either agent
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared workspaces
Review vendor retention settings before use
Use synthetic or masked datasets for joint workflows
Separate compliance-sensitive tasks from agentic IDE sessions
requires-engineering: document and enforce data-handling policy
